mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, كبر مقتا: accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).
His saying أَن تَقولُوا: أن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate); its implied form is "your saying what you do not do is greatly hateful with Allah" (قولكم ما لا تفعلون كبر مقتا عند الله). It is also possible that أن is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is that you say" (هو أن تقولوا). In كبر there is an agent pronoun, i.e. "the hatefulness is great as hatefulness" (كبر المقت مقتا); this is among what is implied without prior mention, but it is implied on condition of explanation, so it is explained by مقت. It is good for كبر مقتا to be the khabar of the saying because it has the meaning of blame; its implied form is "your saying what you do not do is blameworthy", and His saying كبر مقتا has taken the place of "blameworthy" — just as you say زيد نعم رجلا ("Zayd, what an excellent man!"), putting زيد in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ with what follows it as its khabar, although there is nothing in it referring back to it; but it is permissible and good because its meaning is praise, so it is as if its implied form were "Zayd is praiseworthy", and your saying نعم رجلا has taken the place of "praiseworthy". So understand it.
His saying صفا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنيان: in the position of a ḥāl of the nominative latent pronoun in يقاتلون, i.e. they fight resembling a solid structure.
His saying وإذ قَالَ عِيسَى: the governing word in إذ is an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember when he said" (واذكر إذ قال).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying مُصدقا وَمُبشرا: two ḥāls (circumstantial) of ʿĪsā (Jesus), upon him be peace.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying تؤمنون بِاللَّه وتجاهدون: according to al-Mubarrad, its wording is the wording of a statement and its meaning is command, as if He said "believe and strive" (آمنوا وجاهدوا); for that reason He said يغفر لكم ويدخلكم in the jussive, because it is the apodosis of the command; so it is construed according to the meaning. What indicates that is that in the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is آمنوا, as a command. Others said: تؤمنون and تجاهدون are an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to what precedes it; it is as if, when He said, Exalted is He, هل أدلكم على تجارة, it was not known what the trade was, so He explained it by faith and striving, and it was known that the trade is faith and striving. On this view يغفر is the apodosis of the question, construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is "Will you believe in Allah and strive? He will forgive you", since He has explained the trade by faith and striving, so it is the two of them, and it is as if they had been uttered in a position after هل; so the apodosis is construed according to that meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: يغفر is the apodosis of the question. If he meant this sense, it is good; if he did not mean it, that is not permissible, because forgiveness is not made necessary by the guidance (pointing out) — forgiveness is only made necessary by acceptance and action.
His saying وأخرى تحبونها: أخرى is in the position of the genitive by conjunction with تجارة, i.e. "shall I direct you to another trait which you love?"; this is the doctrine of al-Akhfash, and you put نصر in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "that is help" (ذلك نصر) or "it is help" (هي نصر). Al-Farrāʾ said أخرى is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the implied form according to him being "and you have another trait" (ولكم خلة أخرى); this is the choice of al-Ṭabarī, and he argued for it from His saying نصر وفتح in the nominative, as a badal (substitute) of أخرى.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying ظَاهِرين: accusative as the khabar (predicate) of أصبح, and the pronoun is its noun.
